reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 16 close and not stale: SPX down 5.46% from its 120-day high, 3.2% below its 50-day but still 1.01% above its 200-day; SMH down 31.25% from its high and NVDA down 35.84%, both BELOW_ZONE_2 (SMH $461.90 vs Zone 2 $470-505, NVDA $156.14 vs Zone 2 $175-185); VIX 22.91, under the 25 stand-down line; HY OAS 3.23, calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4 (credit calm only).
reaction.invalidation: NVDA beats tonight and closes above $185 (Zone 2 top) with SMH above $505 and the tally at 3 of 4 or better — that would prove the Watch stance wrong and move the posture to Probe/Add.

reaction.trapRisk: The first bounce is the trap: NVDA RSI 22.7 and SMH 17.18% below its 50-day invite a violent snap-back, most likely into the SMH $580-600 / SPX $7,750-7,820 failure zone, where it can fail and resume the decline. Entries change accordingly — no chasing the first bounce, no sizing on a single green day; only a close above the failure zone, or a second low that holds after a failed first bounce, counts as confirmation.

strategyPosture: Watch. This is a CORRECTION episode with the AI complex below its buy zones, the mechanical tally at 1 of 4, and NVDA reporting tonight — no new money goes in until a zone print plus tally confirmation re-arms the ladder.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm masks real weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight. The divergence is real and worth tracking precisely because credit conditions can flip — a loose SLOOS print is a snapshot, not a guarantee. The rotation read holds only while HY OAS stays contained and the laggards stay confined to the AI complex.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read says ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER. Mag7 names average 18.56% below their 52-week highs against SPY only 5.3% below its high — a 13.26-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). AAPL, the strongest Mag7 name, sits just 2.2% off its high while NVDA is 35.8% off its high. Credit is calm: HY OAS 3.23.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad selloff: SPX closed Monday at 7,416.59, down 1.92% on the day and 5.46% below its 120-day high, with QQQ down 2.24% and IWM down 2.06% the same day.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or the Mag7-to-SPY divergence gap widening past 20 points would turn rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: Revenue growth does not set a floor by itself — multiples can keep compressing while the circular-finance and succession questions stay unresolved, and NVDA at $156.14 is already below its $175 Zone 2 floor. The setup is real but the timing is not: a DATA_AHEAD theme with no zone occupancy is a watchlist, not an entry. The dislocation list is dominated by SENTIMENT_DRIVEN declines (36 dislocations), which is exactly the mix that rewards patience over chasing the first bounce.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue prints run the other way. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 35.8% below its high with RSI 22.7 — deeply oversold. AVGO revenue is up 55% with the stock 32.6% off its high; LRCX revenue is up 131.3% with the stock 51.9% off its high; DDOG revenue is up 27.7% with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow, while the stock is 42.5% off its high. DDOG scores 84 (tier A) on the conviction screen, ONTO 81, AVGO 81.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market has priced the AI complex as a broken trade: SMH is down 31.25% from its 120-day high and 15.78% over 20 days, NVDA is down 35.84% from its high and 28.08% over 20 days, and the circular-finance story dominates the tape.
themes.watchFor: NVDA closing back above $175 (Zone 2 floor) after tonight's earnings would re-arm the zone; a close below $140 deepens the dislocation.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying at the trough (VST $1.17M, KTOS $0.2M) and the structural demand flag argue the theme is not dead, only repriced. But the revenue inflection for VST reads STABLE_OR_DECLINING, not recovery — the insiders are buying a trough, not a confirmed turn. Treat any bounce as a repricing pause until a demand print confirms.
themes.dataAnchor: Over one month: SMR down 26.25%, CCJ down 18.76%, OKLO down 17.05%, GEV down 16.2%, VST down 14.35%, BWXT down 14.5% on the month and 51.6% off its 52-week high. VST sits 31.2% below its high at $130.16 with RSI 44.1, yet still scores 83 on conviction with $1.17M of insider buying at the trough and a structural demand inflection flagged active. The only high-materiality news item in the input is a stale TMDX earnings miss from May 6 — there is no fresh fundamental catalyst for this leg down.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the hot theme unwinds
themes.narrative: Nuclear and AI-power names were priced as the next leg of the AI buildout — the story ran ahead of any contracted demand, and the unwind is now the sharpest in the tape.
themes.watchFor: VST's revenue inflection upgrading to RECOVERY, plus two consecutive closes without new lows, would change the read.

themes.counterRead: Software derating can persist while rates stay high — the 10-year is 5.15% with a real 10-year of 2.95% — because duration-heavy growth names are the first to reprice when the curve stays elevated. DDOG's tier-A score (84) and ONTO's (81) are the cleanest DATA_AHEAD setups in the screen, but both carry a 'no earnings before 2027-01-19' timing status, so there is no near-term catalyst to force the re-rate.
themes.dataAnchor: The growth is still there. DDOG revenue is up 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin and 29.2% free-cash-flow margin; NOW's 1-month trend is -30% while its dislocation is flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not a fundamental break; ONTO revenue is up 41.5% with a 29.8% free-cash-flow margin. The 1-month laggard list is led by names whose declines are sentiment, not earnings: RDDT -39.94%, HIMS -33.7%, COIN -31.05%.
themes.label: Software / SaaS: growth stocks derated
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is being sold as if demand is rolling over: NOW is 43.2% below its 52-week high with RSI 30.2, DDOG 42.5% below with RSI 28.5, HUBS 43.0% below, SNOW 27.0% below.
themes.watchFor: A 10-year close below 5.0% plus DDOG holding above $170 would mark the derating as exhausted.

themes.counterRead: Alignment cuts both ways: when narrative and data agree on a washout, the washout can still overshoot — BTC was up 0.34% Monday and DOGE up 1.23% while the rest of the complex fell, the first non-confirmation. Do not read agreement as a bottom call; the leverage is still working its way out.
themes.dataAnchor: Over one month: CONL down 55.28%, COIN down 31.05%, ETH down 22.26%, IBIT down 20.26%, BTC down 19.5%, BMNR down 24.42%, TQQQ down 21.3%. BMNR fell 6.88% on Monday alone and TQQQ fell 6.93%. The portfolio holds BMNR, TQQQ, CONL and DOGE — all four are in the month's laggard list, so the book is taking the unwind directly.
themes.label: Crypto and leverage unwind
themes.narrative: The leveraged-crypto complex is unwinding hard, and the narrative and the data agree: this is a leverage washout, not a single-name story.
themes.watchFor: BTC holding above its 200-week average on a weekly close, or COIN stabilizing above its 1-month trend, would mark the unwind as done.
